title: Detachable Fiber Connectors Pose New Challenges For Photonics
gist: CPO and NPO move optics from faceplate pluggables into or near the package to cut SerDes power, but attaching fiber is the unsolved bottleneck: V-grooves and pigtails don't suit high-volume tray handling, test and serviceability, and detachable connectors (Senko, Intel Foundry, Amkor approaches, magnetic options) are multiplying with no standard yet.

insights.claim: Co-packaged optics (CPO) and near-packaged optics (NPO) aim to cut system power and latency by eliminating long SerDes-driven electrical runs from processors/switches to faceplate pluggable transceivers, bringing fiber onto the board interior or into the package.
insights.speaker: Bryon Moyer
insights.so_what: Structural shift of optical value from faceplate pluggable modules toward package-level optics and fiber-attach suppliers.
insights.locator: CPO aims to reduce system power by eliminating

insights.claim: Ayar Labs frames CPO as a lever on AI 'token economics' because compute, memory and data movement are the major bottlenecks, and step-change 5x-10x hardware gains require new interconnect hardware.
insights.speaker: Bryon Moyer
insights.so_what: Optical I/O vendors are pitching CPO on AI cost-per-token, tying their TAM to AI cluster economics.
insights.quote: “CPO unlocks the token economics that everyone cares about,” said Chandrasekar.
insights.locator: CPO aims to reduce system power by eliminating

insights.claim: In near-term CPO architectures the laser stays outside the package and remains pluggable on the faceplate, because the laser is the highest reliability risk and runs hot.
insights.speaker: Bryon Moyer
insights.so_what: External/pluggable laser sources remain a durable socket even as optical engines move in-package.
insights.quote: “What we are focused on has the laser on the faceplate, because the laser is the highest reliability risk,”
insights.locator: One reason for maintaining faceplate pluggables

insights.claim: AIM Photonics says CPO is just another variant of advanced packaging, sharing all its challenges except fiber coupling and moving the photonic IC (PIC) close to the target chip; CPO gets the bulk of near-term optical development effort.
insights.speaker: Bryon Moyer
insights.so_what: Advanced-packaging OSATs and fiber-coupling specialists are positioned to capture CPO value; fiber coupling is the differentiating hard problem.
insights.locator: CPO is yet another variant of advanced packaging

themes.theme: Fiber attach: V-groove and shoreline limits

insights.claim: Today's dominant V-groove fiber attach (fibers exiting the photonic die edge) works at low volume but lacks modularity for high-volume automation and offers no rework if a fiber breaks during board assembly, pushing the industry toward detachable connectors.
insights.speaker: Bryon Moyer
insights.so_what: Watch detachable optical connector suppliers as an enabling bottleneck for CPO volume ramps.
insights.quote: “When being assembled onto a board, if one of them breaks, there’s no rework. People are generally thinking in terms of detachables and moving away from V-grooves.”
insights.locator: Today, fibers typically are placed using well-established V-groove

insights.claim: Fiber attach consumes die 'shoreline': a 10 µm fiber core becomes 125 µm with cladding, so edge-attaching even 16 fibers uses a lot of perimeter real estate; vertical (surface) coupling via a 45° mirror opens the whole chip area for connections.
insights.speaker: Bryon Moyer
insights.so_what: Bandwidth density of CPO is gated by fiber-coupling geometry; vertical coupling designs scale better.
insights.quote: “The fiber diameter is 10 µm, but you have all the cladding around it, making it 125 µm,”

insights.claim: Intel Foundry notes vertical fiber coupling can collide with heat sinks/thermal solutions on top of the package, so supporting both vertical and lateral coupling gives designers flexibility based on thermal constraints.
insights.speaker: Bryon Moyer
insights.so_what: Thermal-optical co-design trade-offs will differentiate foundry/packaging offerings for CPO.
insights.quote: “When you send it vertically, you may get in the way of your thermal solution,”
insights.locator: But vertical approaches must avoid any heat sinks

insights.claim: Pigtailed photonic chips break standard tray-based automated pick-and-place and test handling (few parts per tray, dangling fibers, manual connection), so Amkor prefers detachable connectors built into the package for high-volume manufacturing.
insights.speaker: Bryon Moyer
insights.so_what: CPO HVM economics depend on making optical packages handle like ordinary chips — a gating factor for CPO adoption timelines.
insights.quote: “If you have a pigtail, it’s very difficult to wrap that pigtail around and put it in a tray, and you probably won’t have many parts on the tray,”

insights.claim: Despite their HVM drawbacks, pigtails are still more common than in-package detachable connectors because the industry is making incremental changes, per Synopsys.
insights.speaker: Bryon Moyer
insights.so_what: Expect a slower-than-hyped transition to pigtail-less CPO packaging.
insights.quote: “Pigtails are probably still more common because people are trying to make incremental changes,”

insights.claim: STL's CTO says terminating fibers at package scale must be low cost, high yield and repeatable across hundreds of connections, with zero dust tolerance and survival through high-temperature reflow.
insights.speaker: Bryon Moyer
insights.so_what: Yield on fiber termination is a hidden cost driver for CPO modules.
insights.quote: “Terminating a fiber is complex,” said Badri Gomatam, CTO of STL.
insights.locator: Scaling volumes also must address the assembly

insights.claim: Active optical alignment is a slow six-degree-of-freedom problem; micro-optics (lenses over optical TSVs in vertical or edge coupling) and passive mechanical alignment (Senko's snap-on connector plus screws) are increasingly used to tolerate misalignment.
insights.speaker: Bryon Moyer
insights.so_what: Passive-alignment connector IP reduces assembly/test time and is a potential moat.
insights.locator: Today, this is done through active alignment

insights.claim: Magnetic fiber connectors (like Apple's iPhone connectors) are being considered for system-level fiber attach, but some are easily damaged and stronger magnets may disturb nearby MRAM, so any magnetic approach will likely need a mechanical latch.
insights.speaker: Bryon Moyer
insights.so_what: Magnetic CPO connectors are early and carry board-level placement risks; not yet an investable standard.
insights.locator: It’s one thing to perform alignment during assembly

insights.claim: Permanent fiber attach (fusing or fixed pigtails) undermines RAS serviceability: a fiber broken in shipment or a failed photonics chip forces scrapping the entire expensive module or server, so connectors must be detachable.
insights.speaker: Bryon Moyer
insights.so_what: Detachability shifts CPO cost-of-failure; buyers (hyperscalers) will demand it.
insights.quote: “You need to make it detachable because if you permanently attach it and the fiber breaks, you have to fail the entire module out, which is very expensive,”

insights.claim: Senko and Advantest developed a tungsten-carbide test connector that mates passively with Senko's LEGO-like connector, avoiding active alignment, and Senko demonstrated 10,000 matings with very little loss variation.
insights.speaker: Bryon Moyer
insights.so_what: Test-equipment readiness (Advantest) for CPO is progressing; watch ATE vendors' optical test exposure.
insights.quote: “We demonstrated 10,000 matings with very little variation in the loss [through the connection],”
insights.locator: Critically, the connection doesn’t require active alignment

insights.claim: Meta published a serviceability/reliability study of CPO devices showing 10,000 hours of constant use without degradation of signal integrity or performance, per Synopsys.
insights.speaker: Bryon Moyer
insights.so_what: Hyperscaler reliability data reduces a key adoption objection to CPO.
insights.locator: The connectors themselves must be reliable enough

insights.claim: There is no standard for CPO/NPO fiber connectors: numerous bespoke pigtail designs exist, no pigtail-less approach is proven at volume, and varying customer requirements complicate standardization; RAND licensing and MSAs will be needed to remove a major photonics volume barrier.
insights.speaker: Bryon Moyer
insights.so_what: Lack of a connector standard is a gating risk on CPO volume timing; a winning MSA/standard would be a catalyst for connector vendors.
insights.locator: Connector attachment is a textbook case

insights.claim: Senko aims to make its package-attached receptacle a common chip interface and sell the cover plate to any fiber-array-unit (FAU) manufacturer.
insights.speaker: Bryon Moyer
insights.so_what: Connector vendors are racing to own the de facto interface — a platform play in CPO.
insights.quote: “Our vision is to take the receptacle part [that gets attached to the package], make that a common interface of the chip, and then sell the cover plate to any FAU manufacturer.”
